HomePage.title: Marie-Eve Musy
HomePage.heroAlt: Marie-Eve Musy, journalist and TV presenter
HomePage.intro: I host two cultural radio shows. Beyond presenting, I also handle much of the production work (finding topics, defining the angle, choosing guests and reaching out to them).

midiBascule.title: Midi Bascule
midiBascule.lead: The show airs live every Friday from noon to 1pm on Radio Vostok, before going online on radiobascule.ch as a podcast.
paragraphs: In 2020, the Théâtre Forum Meyrin teamed up with independent radio station Vostok to launch the Radio Bascule podcast platform. It proved so popular that, a year later, a weekly cultural show was born. Broadcast live on Vostok, it's called Midi Bascule.
I've been part of the adventure since it launched. At first as a columnist, I wrote psycho-humorous pieces about emotions, then read them live on air.
After six months in that role, I was offered the chance to take over as host, which I happily accepted. Alongside two columnists, I welcome two or three guests, depending on the episode.

One guest joins us in the studio for the full hour, while the others check in for a few minutes by phone or voice message. Together – sometimes with a feature report thrown in – we explore a cultural shift currently underway.

cultureMag.title: Culture Mag’
cultureMag.lead: This monthly show airs in audio on Radio Lac and in video on One TV. It's also available online for catch-up viewing.
paragraphs: In September 2022, the City of Geneva launched its new cultural show in partnership with Media One. This group, for whom I had already produced summer segments, entrusted me with the role of host.

We review regional news and host a panel discussion with guests. This enhanced agenda also features two recurring segments produced by the Musée d'art et d'histoire and the Geneva Municipal Libraries.

BiographiePage.title: Biography
BiographiePage.heroAlt: Marie-Eve Musy in a Geneva metro corridor
BiographiePage.lead: Actress, TV presenter, author and now journalist, I love exploring different fields. My career path has mostly been guided by discovery and new challenges.
paragraphs: Marie-Eve Musy was born and raised in Geneva. The drama classes she started at age 8 led her to perform in professional shows and TV series as a teenager. After completing her baccalaureate, she moved to Paris to train in dramatic arts. On graduating from the Cours Florent, she was selected for the sought-after Prix Olga Horstig.

On the big screen, she appears in the casts of Opération Casablanca by Laurent Nègre, Bob et Les Sex Pistaches (Yves Matthey) and Les Petits flocons (Joséphine de Meaux). She plays the lead in the short films Myrtille and I swear. On stage, she has notably appeared in Les trois soeurs (directed by Eric Devanthéry), La mère (directed by Pietro Musillo) and Wagner's Ring Cycle staged by the Salzburg Marionette Theatre (in Paris and Brussels).

She also works in television as an actress (RTS, TF1) and as a presenter. For six years, she hosted shows on the Canal group's first youth channel, where she helped write some of the sketches — her first steps into writing.

As a recipient of a grant from the Swiss Authors' Society (SSA), she wrote a first hybrid show blending emotion, humour and dance around gender inequality. Jean-Luc Barbezat and Gaspard Boesch co-directed dégenre, in which she stars alongside dancer Vivien Hochstätter. The success of its 2019 Geneva premiere led to a tour.
Alongside this, she has hosted events such as the Geneva International Film Festival (GIFF) and accompanied the film Salvataggio on its preview tour, with screenings followed by panel discussions.

In September 2021, Marie-Eve joined the radio show Midi Bascule with psycho-humorous columns. She took over as host of the weekly show in 2022. Since last autumn, she has also presented Culture Mag’ on One TV and Radio Lac.

EcriturePage.title: Writing
EcriturePage.heroAlt: Marie-Eve Musy on stage in the show dégenre
EcriturePage.lead: As a recipient of a grant from the Swiss Authors' Society, I wrote the show dégenre in 2018. I cherish the freedom of tone that writing offers. I also use my pen to craft sketches and radio columns.
EcriturePage.intro: In 2018, after more than fifteen years of bringing other people's stories to life, I wanted to write my own text — the show I dreamed of performing, which didn't yet exist. Using my pen gave me a freedom I cherish, and one I keep when writing my columns.

degenre.title: Dégenre
degenre.lead: Marie-Eve Musy plays with reversals. She brings her dream man on stage and has fun objectifying him while recounting her own personal stories.
degenre.paragraph: In search of harmony, she leads us into a reflection on the notion of gender. Between solo performance, duo (two people share the stage but only one speaks), humour and dance, this show is a genuine one-off.

quotes.text: Delicate, joyful, and full of hope.
quotes.author: An audience member

quotes.text: As its double-meaning title suggests, dégenre deconstructs stereotypes as much as theatrical forms. Comedy tempers personal anecdotes that reveal the ordinary violence of sexism, while dance sketches out a new balance in relationships between women and men.
quotes.author: Le Courrier

degenre.coverAlt: Cover of Marie-Eve Musy's book dégenre

chroniques.title: The columns
chroniques.lead: Talking about your emotions is supposedly good for your health. So I decided to list them and dissect them, one by one (sometimes they even come in pairs!).
paragraphs: I naturally add a few personal experiences of my own. I like to think I'm not the only one going through intense moments, so why not defuse them together?
Because, really, you don't need the adjective «hyper» to be sensitive. Nor a pair of breasts, for that matter.
I've heard that the suicide rate among men is three times higher than among women, partly because, as children, they're taught not to open up.
So, will you have a dash of indignant anger, or a pinch of empathetic sadness?

ActingPage.title: Acting
ActingPage.lead: Film, TV and web series, theatre & short films — I've worked in Switzerland and across Europe.
ActingPage.intro: I enjoy performing on stage as much as on a film set. Both approaches have their own qualities that interest me. My choices are mostly guided by the people behind a project and the role I get to play.
